result:
Memo submitted. Summary of what I found:

**Flux lines meeting the >10% and >$5,000 test (US, Mar vs Feb):**

| Acct | Line | Feb | Mar | Δ$ | Δ% | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5000 | Hosting & Infrastructure | 31,301.80 | 40,948.20 | +9,646.40 | +30.8% | ✅ Holds up |
| 6300 | Travel | 785.40 | 7,158.41 | +6,373.01 | +811% | ❌ Does not hold up |
| 6400 | Marketing Programs | 7,898.14 | 29,686.00 | +21,787.86 | +276% | ⚠️ Not verified |

**Hosting (5000)** – Recurring Stackline production hosting is flat ($31,148 vs $31,302). The whole increase is **JE-00258**, a $9,800 one-time Stackline data-migration invoice, AP-sourced with support attached. Non-recurring; only judgment call is whether any of it is capitalizable.

**Travel (6300)** – The four card transactions total $858 (in line with February). The variance is entirely **JE-00300**, a $6,300 round-dollar *manual* entry "Travel reimbursement – T. Vance" posted 3/29 straight against operating cash with **no support**. That's 88% of the month's travel. I don't consider this explained; it needs an expense report and receipts, confirmation the cash actually cleared, and possibly reclass to Employee Advances (1450) if it's an advance rather than incurred travel. I was unable to file the `flag_exception` call before the tool budget ran out, so the memo serves as the flag.

**Marketing (6400)** – I ran out of tool-call budget before the ledger detail came back. It's the largest movement in the flux and is called out in the memo as an open, high-priority item.

**Below-threshold items worth noting:** March depreciation (6800) and bank fees (6900) both show $0 versus their normal run-rate — those entries appear not yet posted, not a real variance.

No entries were posted, reversed, or matched. If you can re-open the budget, my next batch would be: 6400 Feb/Mar ledger detail, `get_transaction JE-00300`, unmatched bank lines in 1000 for ~$6,300, the US close checklist, and the exception flag on JE-00300.
